items.gist: The earth tattva is purified by water, and tattvas become Shiva through mutual mixing; separateness is mala, so mere karma destruction does not liberate.
Purification proceeds from water through fire, space, and consciousness, then the kalā tattva is purified and the arm-bond is cut.
The karma bond is burned with a full offering in the fire of mantra, and the burnt bond becomes residual like Shiva.
All good and bad karma is offered, then the māyā throat-bond and, if seedless initiation is needed, the samaya bond are burned.
Devotion to guru, deity, and scripture is required, and after māyā purification the vidyā śakti is invoked for the Sadāśiva stage.
The śikhā bond is cut and the āṇava impurity burned, after which the student bathes and the teacher performs purification.
After the āṇava impurity is burned, the student contemplates all knowables as identified with his body and prāṇa, then offers to pure Śiva.
The Trīśira tantra describes complete filling with nectar rising from the root, calming the faculties.
The Pūrvaśāstra method unifies Śiva, Śakti, self, student, ghee, and fire, leading to dvādaśānta and freedom from animal bondage.
If bhoga is desired after bodily death, the union is repeated with full offerings in the relevant tattva.
Dīkṣā is seed-bearing or seedless; seedless is for the weak or when śaktipāta arises, and it purifies samaya bonds.
Tattvas are left from feet to head until subtle niṣkala remains, but in seeded dīkṣā samaya bonds are not purified.
In seeded dīkṣā the guru creates pure tattvas for residual function, by full offering, kumbha abhiṣeka, meditation, or full abhiṣeka.
Earth and other elements become Śiva, tanmātras become blissful, and all impurity is removed.
The senses, mind, and six kañcukas are purified in one who is established in Śiva.
The pure person attains Śiva-nature, and by creation of pure tattvas the student becomes that, as stated in Mālinīvijayottara.
Senses bind when restrained and liberate when freed; their pure and impure modes are distinguished.
The vidyāguru states rules for dīkṣā with all mantras, and kriyās differ by aparā or parā according to the stage.
Offering counts double and quadruple across paths, reaching sixty in tritattva and one hundred eight in ekatattva.
